clue.text: Government agency that minister and a few others know about?

definitions.meaning: the state's intelligence organisation, such as MI6 in Britain

definitions.text: that minister and a few others know about?
definitions.meaning: a church service that only the officiating clergyman and a handful of others are aware of would be a hidden act of worship

explanation.surface: A question about which state body is known only to a government minister and a small inner circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a politician, which fits the spy-agency picture, but in the second reading it is a clergyman leading worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence agencies such as MI6 are commonly called this; the second sense is a church rite held in private.

clue.text: It's not just an option for catering students!

definitions.text: It's not just an option for catering students!

parts.words: It's not just an option for catering students!
parts.note: the clue pretends to describe a cookery module, while the real phrase is a degree that alternates study with periods of work placement

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a certain programme is available to more than trainee cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this name is given to a degree in which college terms are layered between spells of industrial placement, like filling between bread; nothing to do with food.
explanation.definitionFit: A study programme interleaving academic terms with work experience, which the clue jokingly links to catering through its lunchtime name.

clue.text: Boxed disc covering a period

indicators.note: covering means the disc's letters wrap around the period's letters

parts.note: CD, compact disc
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A boxed CD set spanning one era of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut in a cage or boxed in are both ways of being confined.

clue.text: Come in quietly and get promoted in business organisation

parts.note: to come in is to enter
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to get promoted is to rise in rank

explanation.surface: Advice on slipping unobtrusively into a firm and climbing its ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A company or business venture is also called an enterprise, a common synonym.

clue.text: Naughty date and Mrs may get hurt

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving letters, so the words date and Mrs are rearranged

explanation.surface: A risqué liaison between a date and a married woman might end in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' scrambles DATE and MRS together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have smarted is to have stung or felt sharp pain, a synonym for hurt.

clue.text: Rex, having married, recovered

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king
allied means joined or united, as in a marriage

explanation.surface: A king named Rex bounced back after his wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient or market that has rallied has bounced back or regained strength.

clue.text: Home central America? His was further south

parts.note: being in means being at home
CA is the abbreviation for Central America

explanation.surface: Asking if home lies in Central America, then noting one man's lay further south.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: 'his' home was south of Central America, in Peru, so the person meant is one of the Andean empire's people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean empire's people lived in Peru and neighbouring lands, south of the isthmus.

clue.text: After sloshing around I had clean dish

indicators.note: sloshing around suggests the letters of I had clean being churned up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook describing a meal made after splashing around while washing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in sauce, a type of dish.

clue.text: Show surprise as something hairy moves

definitions.meaning: to express astonishment with a facial expression
literally lifting the strip of hair above the eye

explanation.surface: Signalling astonishment with a twitch of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the line of hair over one eye is the classic gesture of disbelief or astonishment.

clue.text: Near beginning of the autumn when it gets dark

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: beginning of tells you to take only the opening letter of the word the

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Autumn days, when darkness comes early.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the time at day's end as darkness descends.

clue.text: Old clown needs a drink

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown of mid-20th-century Britain

explanation.surface: A retired circus performer needs refreshment.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown in Britain from the 1930s to the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Bird to go aimlessly, missing north

indicators.note: missing means the letter for north is left out of the word

parts.note: to wander is to go aimlessly

explanation.surface: A bird drifting about without a sense of direction, lacking north.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons, sandpipers and other long-legged shorebirds are all called by this name.

clue.text: Grind? Put right finally with lubrication

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word right

parts.note: oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: Fixing a grinding machine by adding some lubrication at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grind' looks like a mechanical noise to be fixed with oil, but it means hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard monotonous labour is called grind or drudgery.

clue.text: Girl is to appear in script

indicators.note: to appear in means the word is is placed inside the abbreviation for script

parts.note: MS, manuscript, a handwritten script

explanation.surface: A girl is cast in a play's script.
explanation.definitionFit: A young unmarried woman is addressed with this title.

clue.text: Poet of many words, mate!

parts.note: something of many words is long
fellow means companion or mate

explanation.surface: A friendly remark that a poet is wordy.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was the American poet of 'The Song of Hiawatha'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 19th-century American author of Hiawatha was a renowned poet.

clue.text: Like badly cooked food getting woman in house embarrassed

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman who works in a house
red, as an embarrassed face blushes

explanation.surface: A housewife blushing over food she has burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British term for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Food burnt black from overcooking is scorched in this way.

clue.text: Degradation in a place below stairs

parts.note: a basement is the floor below ground level, reached by going downstairs

explanation.surface: Humiliating work as a servant in the cellar quarters of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below stairs' also suggests the servants' world of old British houses, fitting the picture of humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being humbled or lowered in dignity is a state of humiliation.

clue.text: I love to appear in a play or a picture

indicators.note: to appear in means I and love are placed inside the word for a play

parts.note: a drama is a play
O, zero, a score of love in tennis

explanation.surface: An actor declaring a love of appearing in either theatre or film.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-dimensional model scene, often in a museum, is a type of picture.

clue.text: Support for the car driver

parts.note: reads as backing for a motorist, but describes the frame on which a car is built

explanation.surface: Help offered to someone who drives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' looks like moral support for a motorist; it is the structural framework carrying the car's body and engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's base frame, carrying body and running gear, is its structural support.

clue.text: Release not charged for — leading group

indicators.note: leading means the group word goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: a set is a group
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: Something given away at no cost to the frontrunning band.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate or let go of someone is to release them.

clue.text: Wealthy person of little good taken in by fellow mischief-maker

indicators.note: taken in by means the letter for good goes inside the word for fellow

parts.note: a man is a fellow
G is the short form for good
Ate was the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A rich man with little virtue is fooled by a troublemaking companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon of business or industry is a rich and powerful figure.

clue.text: A German, well-organised as an administrator

indicators.note: well-organised suggests putting the letters of A German into a new order

explanation.surface: A German is well-organised as a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the stereotype of German efficiency.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone running a business or department is its boss or administrator.

clue.text: Part of eye picks out some mauve area

indicators.note: picks out some says the answer is a run of letters taken from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An eye's coloured portion seeming to show a patch of mauve.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'picks out' in the definition, but the definition is only 'Part of eye'; 'picks out some' is the hidden-word signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigmented middle layer of the eyeball, including the iris, is an anatomical part.

clue.text: On return captures a gun

indicators.note: on return means the word for captures is read backwards

parts.note: nets means catches or captures

explanation.surface: Coming back, someone seizes a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: The STEN was a British submachine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A light British submachine gun of the 1940s is a firearm.

clue.text: Ireland rejected by English? It's weird

indicators.note: by means the English abbreviation sits next to the other piece
rejected means the word for Ireland is turned back to front

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Ireland snubbed by the English, which seems strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncanny or spooky is strange in an unsettling way.

clue.text: Artist man thought highly of

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: An artist whom someone admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well regarded or esteemed means being highly valued.

clue.text: Piece of evidence rod left hidden

indicators.note: hidden means the letter for left is tucked inside the word for rod

parts.note: a cue is the rod used in snooker or billiards

explanation.surface: A detective's find: a rod left concealed at the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint that helps detectives solve a mystery is a lead or piece of evidence.

clue.text: Former political leader is less than 100% iron

definitions.meaning: David ..., leader of Britain's Liberal Party from 1976 to 1988
an alloy that is mostly iron with a little carbon

explanation.surface: A one-time party boss described as not quite made of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: David Steel led the British Liberal Party; the alloy is mostly iron with carbon added.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Liberal Party leader's surname; also an alloy chiefly of iron with some carbon.

clue.text: The governor — one to ensure good time-keeping?

definitions.meaning: a device controlling speed or flow in a machine
the mechanism in a clock that adjusts its rate

explanation.surface: Asking whether the person in charge is the one who makes sure everyone is punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: A control device in an engine or a clock adjusting speed or rate; also an official supervisor.

clue.text: Rowdier myth we transformed into operetta

indicators.note: transformed suggests the letters of Rowdier myth we are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy legend turned into a light musical stage work.
explanation.walkthrough: Lehár's 1905 operetta is about a rich widow in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár's famous Viennese light opera is an operetta.
